title: Feature Scaling — Choose the Right Ruler
key_insight: Min-max scaling uses the observed ends. Standard scaling uses the average and spread. Robust scaling uses middle ranks and resists extreme outliers.
body:
## Choose the Right Ruler

Most values cluster normally, but one huge outlier stretches the range. A zero-to-one ruler squeezes ordinary values into a tiny space.

Min-max scaling uses the observed ends. Standard scaling uses the average and spread. Robust scaling uses middle ranks and resists extreme outliers.

Trees usually do not need scaling because their split order survives a change of units. KNN, SVM, and gradient-based models often do.
common_mistakes: Fitting the scaler before the train/test split.
Using min-max scaling without checking extreme outliers.
Centering a huge sparse matrix until it becomes dense.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Choose the Right Ruler” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Distance methods and gradient-based models can be distorted or slowed by mismatched feature units.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Choose the Right Ruler” story, explain Feature Scaling without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
